1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls requireAuth, and authenticatedSession rejects sessions whose accountId does not match account.id, so settings access is bound to the signed-in owner (trivially so, since only one demo account exists).

2.why: The TOTP secret and recovery codes are tied to the single account record and verified against it, and no user identifier is accepted from the client (bodies containing accountId/userId are rejected), so a code could not be reused for another user — though the single-account design makes this untestable.

3.why: The /api/mfa/verify handler sets account.mfaEnabled=true without deleting or rotating any session, so the existing session id (and any other previously issued authenticated sessions in the map) remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: account.encryptedSecret and account.encryptedRecoveryCodes are stored via encrypt() using AES-256-GCM with a random IV and auth tag, never in plain text.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, IVs and recovery codes all derive from node:crypto randomBytes, a CSPRNG (recovery codes have slight modulo bias but remain cryptographically seeded).

6.why: The only cookie is mfa_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict and no localStorage/sessionStorage is used, although the TOTP secret/OTP are held in a JS variable and printed to the DOM/console for the demo.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validCode), JSON content-type/length checks and rejection of unexpected keys constrain all input; no SQL/dynamic queries exist since storage is in-memory.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent/createTextNode/replaceChildren; innerHTML is used only with static literals, and a strict nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' is set.

9.why: The application issues no redirects at all (no Location headers or client navigation), so there is no open-redirect risk but also no explicit allow-list implementation to speak of.

10.why: headers() sets Strict-Transport-Security, a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: cookie() and clearCookie() emit mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict plus Max-Age.

12.why: Errors are generic and stack traces suppressed, but /api/mfa/setup deliberately returns the Base32 TOTP seed and a live OTP in its JSON response, and the client console.logs the secret, OTP and all recovery codes into an on-page log panel.

13.why: TOTP acceptance is limited to a ±1 30-second window with acceptedCounter replay rejection, and recovery codes carry a 30-day expiresAt and are spliced out of storage once consumed.

14.why: failed()/locked() enforce MAX_FAILURES=5 then a 10-minute lockout returning HTTP 429 for both OTP and recovery-code verification, cleared on success.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the pre-auth session and issues a brand-new id, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in authenticatedSession, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie — but the id is not rotated again when MFA is enabled.
